reviewer: Independent native-source visual and anatomical-registration review
scope: Four exact whole native RGBA 2x2 sources for Union A north direction 6 and Confederate A south direction 2 contact/casualty. This accepts sources and their registrations for the bounded normal-Gettysburg v23 opt-in workflow; exports, actual playback and final installation require separate verification.
decision: All sixteen native cells were inspected. The selected Union casualty replacement resolves the broader head/pack concern sufficiently for this opt-in source group. Kit, bearing, limb/head proportions and phase separation are coherent enough to proceed with one independently measured reference per army. Rear contact grip and thrust interpretation remain bounded visual judgments.
referenceMethod: For each army, four independently chosen cap-only ROIs and support-sole-only ROIs give alpha>=64 capTop and exclusive soleGroundY. bodySpan=soleGroundY-capTop. The common reference is the half-up rounded median of those four contact spans and is shared unchanged with that army casualty sheet. The two armies are measured separately; no individual action phase is normalized.
pivotMethod: Each native integer X is manually selected from projected pelvis/torso anatomy. Each Y is the exclusive maximum alpha>=64 pixel row within the independently selected support ROI. Support X may differ from pelvis X; no bounding-box, gun-tip or per-phase-scale pivot is substituted. Forearm/palm supports are used where prone or collapsing body-ground projection is partly occluded.
registrationUncertainty: The selected ROI extrema are exactly reproducible. Semantic projected centre/support interpretation remains approximate at roughly 6-10 native pixels and is not a physical skeleton or fixed planted-foot certification.
capSelectionNote: Union contact cell 1 uses the visible right crown to exclude the adjacent raised hand and rifle; Confederate contact cell 1 uses a sole ROI left of the overlapping bayonet.
proportionAssessment: The corrected Union casualty has slightly smaller head silhouettes in some views but coherent roll, boots and limbs relative to the smaller contact sheet. The Confederate pair retains consistent head, coat, pack and boots through crouch/sprawl foreshortening. Projected contact-span changes are retained rather than judged by a stationary-pose height-spread rule.

rejectedOrWithheldSource.reason: First head/bedroll visibly broader than the small contact partner; held for a whole native redraw. No per-cell export scaling was used.

limitations: Source-only model-assisted acceptance. Native export/actual renderer checks, public playback and exact frozen-candidate installation acceptance remain separate.

Union north forehand/stock placement supports a foreshortened contact interpretation, but the rear grip is partially occluded and the extension can resemble a raised forward guard in a still. Actual motion and transitions must be inspected.
Natural crouch, lunge and prone foreshortening changes projected height and visible proportions. These four poses are not a continuous skeletal rig or anatomy/drill certification.

Low-alpha coloured fringe/noise remains, including nonzero-alpha residues beyond solid silhouettes. The selected sources meet solid alpha64 padding, not a fringe-free or all-background cleanliness certification.
The family remains incomplete: reverse E/W partners (Union east, Confederate west), diagonal contact/fall, Union B and other roles remain outside this source group.
No default promotion, production approval, human usability certification, historical authenticity certification or whole-game quality judgment is granted.
